about: Sources for the sentences added to the six case studies (web/projects/*.html) in round 8. tests/case-studies.test.js reads this file: every factual sentence on a case study must be published on the homepage, a lab page (web/lab/*.html) or the build trace (web/trace/build-trace.json), or be listed here. Each entry must still appear on its page. For homepage, lab and trace entries every quote must appear in that source, and the status is approved. Résumé entries cannot be checked by the test and stay pending-cesar until Cesar confirms them; he can then set status to approved. 'reworded' means the sentence restates the quoted source in new words; Cesar should read those.

sources.résumé 2026-11: Cesar's résumé of November 2026 (Cesar_Tortolero_Resume_2026-11.html, kept outside the repository)

facts.sentence: How do you give coding agents clear roles, and delivery context they can read but not change?
quote: Clear roles and read-only access to delivery tools
Context they can read, not change.

facts.sentence: I built the workflow: specialist coding subagents, read-only MCP servers for Jenkins and Bitbucket, and a searchable knowledge base compiled automatically from work sessions.
quote: A multi-agent developer workflow.
Specialist coding subagents split the work
Read-only MCP servers give them Jenkins and Bitbucket context, and a searchable knowledge base is compiled automatically from work sessions.
facts.note: "I built" comes from the essay: "The multi-agent workflow I built is set up that way".

facts.sentence: A recorded agent run built two rounds of this site: 52 steps and 16 commits, errors and retries included.

Resume the interrupted orange-box fix
facts.note: 52 = totals.spans; 16 = run.commits; statuses include error (8) and retried (2). Whether this run counts as the Multi-Agent Workflow itself is question 1 in docs/case-study-questions.md.
